author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In a central limit theorem for the number of vertices of the convex hull of a uniform sample from the interior of a convex polygon is derived This is done by approximating the process of vertices of the convex hull by the process of extreme points of a Poisson point process and by considering the latter process of extreme points as a Markov process for a particular parametrization We show that this method can also be applied to derive limit theorems for the boundary length and for the area of the convex hull This extends results of Renyi and Sulanke and Buchta and shows that the boundary length and the area have a strikingly different probabilistic behavior

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We study three estimators for the interval censoring case problem a histogramtype estimator proposed in the maximum likelihood estimator MLE and the smoothed MLE using a smoothing kernel Our focus is on the asymptotic distribution of the estimators at a fixed point The estimators are compared in a simulation study

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We consider the problem of estimating the joint distribution function of the event time and a continuous mark variable when the event time is subject to interval censoring case and the continuous mark variable is only observed in case the event occurred before the time of inspection The nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator in this model is known to be inconsistent We study two alternative smooth estimators based on the explicit inverse expression of the distribution function of interest in terms of the density of the observable vector We derive the pointwise asymptotic distribution of both estimators

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We consider the problem of estimating the joint distribution function of the event time and a continuous mark variable based on censored data More specifically the event time is subject to current status censoring and the continuous mark is only observed in case inspection takes place after the event time The nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator in this model is known to be inconsistent We propose and study an alternative likelihoodbased estimator maximising a smoothed loglikelihood hence called a maximum smoothed likelihood estimator MSLE This estimator is shown to be well defined and consistent and a simple algorithm is described that can be used to compute it The MSLE is compared with other estimators in a small simulation study

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We consider the maximum likelihood estimator of a distribution function in a class of deconvolution models where the known density of the noise variable is of bounded variation This class of noise densities contains in particular bounded decreasing densities The estimator is defined characterized in terms of Fenchel optimality conditions and computed Under appropriate conditions various consistency results for are derived including uniform strong consistency The Canadian Journal of Statistics c Statistical Society of Canada

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper investigates the properties of Brownian motion under the influence of a parabolic drift with a specific focus on the connections to Airy functions We first establish the mathematical framework for modeling Brownian motion with a quadratically varying drift term leading to a new class of stochastic processes that exhibit features influenced by both classical Brownian motion and the unique characteristics of Airy functions Through rigorous analysis we derive explicit solutions for the probability density function and transition probabilities of the modified process revealing the intricate interplay between the drift and the underlying stochastic behavior Furthermore we explore the longterm behavior of the system identifying asymptotic properties and moments that provide insights into the impact of the parabolic drift on the trajectory of the particle Our findings contribute to the broader understanding of stochastic processes influenced by polynomial drifts with potential applications in fields such as finance physics and biological modeling By drawing connections between these two mathematical domains we highlight the richness of the structural relationships that govern complex systems

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of functionals derived from the convex hulls of random points in multidimensional spaces We establish limit theorems that characterize the distributional properties of various functionals applied to convex hulls including the area volume and geometric parameters such as the diameter and the shape characteristics of the hulls formed by sequences of independent and identically distributed random variables Utilizing techniques from geometric probability and large deviation theory we derive conditions under which convergence in distribution occurs for these functionals as the number of points approaches infinity Our results extend existing theoretical frameworks and provide new insights into the statistical properties of convex hulls demonstrating how the distribution of functionals behaves under different dimensional contexts and point distributions Numerical simulations are conducted to support the theoretical findings and illustrate practical implications paving the way for applications in fields such as spatial statistics computational geometry and data analysis

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper introduces a novel framework for estimating the inverse of a cumulative distribution function CDF in the context of current status data utilizing smooth plugin estimators Current status data wherein the exact time of an event is unobservable but the status is known at a given time poses unique challenges for traditional estimation techniques Our approach leverages kernel smoothing methods to create inverse estimators that maintain desirable statistical properties such as consistency and asymptotic normality We present a detailed theoretical analysis of the proposed estimators including biasvariance tradeoffs and convergence rates complemented by simulation studies that illustrate their performance in finite samples Additionally we apply our methodology to a realworld dataset to demonstrate its practical utility and effectiveness compared to existing estimation techniques The findings indicate that smooth plugin inverse estimators outperform conventional methods thereby offering a robust tool for analyzing current status continuous mark models in various applied contexts

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper investigates the properties of the concave majorant of standard Brownian motion a fundamental object in stochastic processes and statistical analysis We develop a framework to analyze the concave majorant as a function of time establishing its relationship with the underlying Brownian path By employing techniques from convex analysis we derive new results concerning the distribution and statistical characteristics of the concave majorant In particular we show that the expectation and variance of the concave majorant can be expressed in terms of the local time of Brownian motion Additionally we explore the asymptotic behavior of the concave majorant as the observation window extends providing insights into its scaling properties Our findings reveal a deeper understanding of the role of the concave majorant in the context of stochastic processes and its implications in various applications including option pricing and risk assessment in finance We conclude with potential extensions of this research to multidimensional Brownian motion and discuss the implications for future studies in probabilistic modeling and statistical inference

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Let S t S be a version of the slope at time t t of the concave majorant of Brownian motion on It is shown that the process S S is the inverse of a pure jump process with independent nonstationary increments and that Brownian motion can be generated by the latter process and Brownian excursions between values of the process at successive jump times As an application the limiting distribution of the L L norm of the slope of the concave majorant of the empirical process is derived

author: Piet Groeneboom

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Interval censoring occurs when the exact value of an observation is not known but rather it is known to lie within a certain interval This phenomenon is common in various fields including survival analysis clinical trials and reliability engineering In this paper we propose new estimators to address the interval censoring problem aiming to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of statistical inference under these constraints We derive maximum likelihood estimators MLEs using both fully parametric and semiparametric frameworks and we assess their performance through asymptotic properties and simulation studies Additionally we introduce a robust Bayesian approach to interval censoring utilizing prior information to refine estimates where data is sparse or heavily censored We compare the proposed estimators to existing methods through extensive simulations under different censoring schemes and sample sizes Our empirical results indicate that our estimators outperform traditional approaches in terms of bias and mean squared error particularly in situations with substantial censoring Finally we present a realworld application to demonstrate the practical utility of our methods in analyzing patient survival data The findings contribute significant advancements to the statistical methodology for handling intervalcensored data providing researchers with improved tools for analysis and inference

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we investigate the consistency of maximum likelihood estimators MLEs within a broad class of deconvolution models which are frequently employed in various fields such as signal processing and biostatistics to estimate underlying distributions from observed convoluted data We establish conditions under which the MLEs converge in probability to the true parameter values as the sample size increases Our results extend existing frameworks by accommodating a wider variety of kernel functions and error distributions including those with heavy tails By employing tools from empirical process theory and leveraging the properties of convex hulls we provide a robust theoretical foundation for the consistency of MLEs in deconvolution contexts Through simulations and real data applications we illustrate the practical implications of our findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of MLEs in recovering the original signal from contaminated observations These results not only contribute to the theoretical understanding of deconvolution estimators but also pave the way for future research in nonparametric inference and robust statistical methodologies

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we investigate the asymptotic behavior of statistics derived from the convex minorants of empirical distribution functions We establish that as the sample size approaches infinity these statistics converge in distribution to a normal distribution under certain regularity conditions By leveraging the properties of convex minorants and the underlying structure of empirical distribution functions we provide a comprehensive framework for analyzing the asymptotic normality of various functionals associated with the convex hulls formed by these minorants Our results extend existing theories in nonparametric statistics and offer new insights into the convergence properties of empirical processes We also present applications of our findings in statistical inference particularly in the context of goodnessoffit tests and estimation methodologies Through simulations we illustrate the finitesample performance of our proposed methods reinforcing the practical significance of our theoretical contributions

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we introduce a novel Maximum Smoothed Likelihood Estimator MSLE tailored for the Current Status Continuous Mark Model a framework that captures incomplete data scenarios commonly encountered in survival analysis and reliability studies Current status data where only the event occurrence is observed at a specific time without information on the exact event time poses significant challenges for traditional estimation techniques Our proposed MSLE leverages smoothing techniques to enhance the likelihood surface mitigating the effects of noise and sampling variability while improving parameter estimation accuracy We derive the theoretical underpinnings of the MSLE ensuring asymptotic properties are established including consistency and asymptotic normality Extensive simulations demonstrate the superior performance of MSLE compared to existing estimation methods particularly in finite sample scenarios Additionally we present a realdata application to illustrate the practical utility of our approach This work provides a robust statistical tool for researchers dealing with current status data paving the way for more accurate inference in related fields

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we investigate the statistical properties of hazard functions focusing on the testing of monotonicity in the context of survival analysis The central contribution is the development of a robust theoretical framework for assessing monotonic behavior in hazard rates derived from censored survival data We derive the asymptotic distribution of a novel test statistic designed to detect deviations from monotonicity rooted in the estimation of hazard functions via nonparametric methods Through a series of simulations we evaluate the performance of our test in terms of power and type I error rates under various models including exponential and Weibull distributions Additionally we provide practical guidelines for application demonstrating the tests utility through realworld datasets Our findings elucidate the nuances of hazard function behavior and offer a rigorous methodology for researchers seeking to understand the implications of monotonicity in survival data The results pave the way for enhanced inferential techniques in the analysis of lifetime data across diverse fields including medicine engineering and social sciences

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We consider the problem of testing equality of functions fj for j J on the basis of J independent samples from possibly different distributions under the assumption that the functions are monotone We provide a uniform approach that covers testing equality of monotone regression curves equality of monotone densities and equality of monotone hazards in the random censorship model Two test statistics are proposed based on Ldistances We show that both statistics are asymptotically normal and we provide bootstrap implementations which are shown to have critical regions with asymptotic level alpha

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We consider the maximum likelihood estimator of a distribution function in a class of deconvolution models where the known density of the noise variable is of bounded variation This class of noise densities contains in particular bounded decreasing densities The estimator is defined characterized in terms of Fenchel optimality conditions and computed Under appropriate conditions various consistency results for are derived including uniform strong consistency The Canadian Journal of Statistics c Statistical Society of Canada

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Two test statistics are introduced to test the null hypotheses that the sampling distribution has an increasing hazard rate on a specified interval These statistics are empirical Ltype distances between the isotonic estimates which use the monotonicity constraint and either the empirical distribution function or the empirical cumulative hazard They measure the excursions of the empirical estimates with respect to the isotonic estimates owing to local nonmonotonicity Asymptotic normality of the test statistics if the hazard is strictly increasing on is established under mild conditions This is done by first approximating the global empirical distance by a distance with respect to the underlying distribution function The resulting integral is treated as sum of increasingly many local integrals to which a central limit theorem can be applied The behavior of the local integrals is determined by a canonical process the difference between the stochastic process x bar right arrow Wx x where W is standard twosided Brownian motion and its greatest convex minorant

author: Piet Groeneboom

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we investigate the problem of testing the equality of two functions subject to monotonicity constraints a scenario frequently encountered in various fields such as economics biology and machine learning Traditional methods for function equality testing often assume independence of the functions properties however in realworld applications monotonicity can significantly influence the comparison results We propose a novel statistical framework that incorporates monotonicity constraints into the hypothesis testing paradigm allowing for a more nuanced evaluation of function equality Our approach leverages nonparametric techniques and introduces a robust test statistic that accounts for the functional forms of the tested functions while maintaining their monotonic properties Through extensive simulations and applications to real datasets we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in reducing Type I and Type II errors relative to conventional testing approaches We also discuss the implications of our findings for practitioners seeking to discern subtle differences between monotonic functions in observational studies Ultimately this study offers a comprehensive statistical approach to evaluating function equality under monotonicity constraints paving the way for future research in this domain

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Groeneboom introduced a jump process that can be used among other things to study the asymptotic properties of the Grenander estimator of a monotone density In this paper we derive the asymptotic normality of a suitably rescaled version of the L error of the Grenander estimator using properties of this jump process

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the L error of the Grenander estimator a widely used nonparametric estimator for monotonic functions We establish the conditions under which the L error converges in distribution to a normal distribution as the sample size approaches infinity Utilizing advanced tools from empirical process theory and the properties of convex functions we derive explicit bounds for the L error and demonstrate that its asymptotic distribution aligns with theoretical predictions Our findings not only enhance the understanding of the Grenander estimators performance in statistical estimation but also provide a framework for assessing its robustness in practical applications We illustrate our theoretical results through simulations reinforcing the practical significance of our findings for statisticians utilizing nonparametric methods in various fields Overall this study contributes to the rich literature on nonparametric estimation by offering new insights into the error characteristics of the Grenander estimator under largesample settings

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we explore the concepts of Bahadur efficiency and smallsample efficiency within the framework of statistical inference Bahadur efficiency provides a measure of the asymptotic optimality of statistical procedures particularly in the context of nonparametric hypothesis testing by comparing the rates of convergence of the null and alternative hypotheses In contrast smallsample efficiency focuses on the performance of estimators and tests under limited sample sizes addressing the discrepancies that can arise between theoretical asymptotic properties and practical applications We present an integrated approach to assess both Bahadur efficiency and smallsample efficiency for a variety of commonly used statistical tests and estimators such as ttests and rankbased tests Through a combination of simulation studies and theoretical derivations we highlight the tradeoffs between the two efficiency measures elucidating scenarios where traditional asymptotic results may fail to provide adequate guidance in finite samples Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of statistical procedures effectiveness promoting the careful consideration of sample size in empirical research The insights provided by this study have significant implications for the design of experiments and the interpretation of statistical results in practice

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we address the challenge of estimating smooth functionals in the presence of interval censoring a prevalent scenario in survival analysis and reliability engineering Building upon our previous work we focus on Case of interval censoring characterized by more complex underlying data structures We derive asymptotically optimal estimation procedures for smooth functionals leveraging advanced techniques from nonparametric statistics and empirical processes Our primary contributions include the establishment of a theoretical framework that describes the asymptotic properties of our estimators including consistency and asymptotic normality We further propose an innovative algorithm that incorporates adaptive bandwidth selection enhancing estimation performance in finite samples The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through extensive simulations and a case study involving realworld survival data highlighting the practical applicability of our results Our findings not only provide a deeper theoretical understanding of smooth functional estimation under interval censoring but also set a foundation for future research in this area

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: For a version of the interval censoring model case in which the observation intervals are allowed to be arbitrarily small we consider estimation of functionals that are differentiable along Hellinger differentiable paths The asymptotic information lower bound for such functionals can be represented as the squared Lnorm of the canonical gradient in the observation space This canonical gradient has an implicit expression as a solution of an integral equation that does not belong to one of the standard types We study an extended version of the integral equation that can also be used for discrete distribution functions like the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator NPMLE and derive the asymptotic normality and efficiency of the NPMLE from properties of the solutions of the integral equations

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive exploration of Chernoffs distribution a significant statistical tool used for modeling the behavior of random variables in various applications including reliability engineering and decision theory We begin by deriving the characteristic properties of Chernoffs distribution highlighting its relation to exponential families and the implications of its momentgenerating function We introduce novel computational techniques that enhance the efficiency of parameter estimation utilizing both maximum likelihood estimation MLE and Bayesian approaches Our methodology incorporates advanced numerical methods and simulation techniques to address potential computational challenges associated with the distribution Furthermore we provide a thorough analysis of the distributions performance through a series of simulation studies demonstrating its applicability in realworld scenarios The paper concludes with a detailed discussion of the implications of Chernoffs distribution in statistical modeling and decisionmaking processes as well as suggestions for future research directions in this area

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: A distribution that arises in problems of estimation of monotone functions is that of the location of the maximum of twosided Brownian motion minus a parabola Using results from the first authors earlier work we present algorithms and programs for computation of this distribution and its quantiles We also present some comparisons with earlier computations and simulations

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper explores the connections between Ulams Problem and Hammersleys Process two prominent topics in the realms of combinatorial mathematics and stochastic processes Ulams Problem which investigates the characteristics and properties of random sequences and their longest increasing subsequences provides a rich framework for understanding various combinatorial structures Meanwhile Hammersleys Process a stochastic model describing the growth of random interfaces offers insights into the probabilistic behavior of such sequences over time We establish a mathematical link between these two areas by demonstrating how the asymptotic behavior of the longest increasing subsequences in Ulams Problem can be analyzed using tools from the theory of Hammersleys Process Through rigorous statistical methods we derive new results concerning the convergence properties and distributional aspects of these subsequences Our findings not only contribute to the theoretical understanding of both topics but also suggest potential applications in fields such as statistical physics and algorithm design The implications of these results pave the way for further research into the intricate interplay between combinatorial structures and stochastic phenomena

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We study nonparametric estimation of the subdistribution functions for current status data with competing risks Our main interest is in the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator MLE and for comparison we also consider a simpler naive estimator Both types of estimators were studied by Jewell van der Laan and Henneman Biometrika but little was known about their large sample properties We have started to fill this gap by proving that the estimators are consistent and converge globally and locally at rate n We also show that this local rate of convergence is optimal in a minimax sense The proof of the local rate of convergence of the MLE uses new methods and relies on a rate result for the sum of the MLEs of the subdistribution functions which holds uniformly on a fixed neighborhood of a point Our results are used in Groeneboom Maathuis and Wellner Ann Statist to obtain the local limiting distributions of the estimators

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We consider the problem of estimating the distribution function the density and the hazard rate of the unobservable event time in the current status model A well studied and natural nonparametric estimator for the distribution function in this model is the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator MILE We study two alternative methods for the estimation of the distribution function assuming some smoothness of the event time distribution The first estimator is based oil a maximum smoothed likelihood approach The second method is based on smoothing the discrete MLE of the distribution function These estimators can be used to estimate the density and hazard rate of the event time distribution based on the plugin principle

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper investigates the large deviations behavior of goodnessoffit statistics focusing on their asymptotic properties in the context of linear combinations of order statistics We establish a framework to analyze how deviations from expected goodnessoffit measures such as the KolmogorovSmirnov Cram rvon Mises and AndersonDarling statistics behave under large sample conditions Utilizing techniques from probability theory and statistical analysis we derive explicit bounds on the tail probabilities of these statistics and their linear combinations Our results reveal significant insights into the distribution and variability of goodnessoffit metrics suggesting that under certain conditions their large deviations can be effectively characterized in terms of the underlying order statistics of the sample This work not only provides theoretical advancements in statistical inference but also offers practical implications for model diagnostics and selection in applied research Ultimately our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the robustness of goodnessoffit tests in the presence of underlying data structures and distributional assumptions

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper introduces Generalized Continuous Isotonic Regression GCIR a novel extension of traditional isotonic regression methodologies tailored for continuous response variables across various distributions Isotonic regression is wellestablished for estimating monotonic relationships but existing frameworks often impose limitations on the type of response data they can handle Our approach generalizes the concept by integrating a broader class of loss functions and accommodating nonparametric strategies to maintain monotonicity We rigorously outline the mathematical foundations of GCIR presenting algorithms for efficient computation and convergence guarantees Key theoretical results demonstrate its consistency and robustness in highdimensional settings alongside simulation studies illustrating improved performance compared to standard isotonic methods Applications in fields such as biostatistics and econometrics are utilized to highlight the practical benefits of GCIR offering insights into the underlying trends of realworld data while maintaining a flexible modeling framework This work paves the way for further advancements in nonparametric regression techniques encouraging researchers to explore the implications of continuous isotonic relationships in diverse datasets

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: The standard isotonic regression of a vectorin Rn is the solution to a least squares projection problem on the cone C of vectors with increasing components in Rn Generalized isotonic regression problems are isotonic optimization problems that seem to be quite different from isotonic regression problems but in fact have the same solution In problems of maximum smoothed likelihood estimation often continuous versions of generalized isotonic regression problems emerge In this paper we show that the solutions to such problems are often given by the relatively simple continuous isotonic regression of a function We illustrate the result using the problem of maximum smoothed likelihood estimation of an increasing hazard function C Elsevier BV

text: Let Ln be the length of the longest increasing subsequence of a random permutation of the numbers n for the uniform distribution on the set of permutations Hammersleys interacting particle process implicit in Hammersley has been used in Aldous and Diaconis to provide a soft hydrodynamical argument for proving that limn infinity ELnrootn We show in this note that the latter result is in fact an immediate consequence of properties of a random dimensional signed measure associated with Hammersleys process

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we investigate the statistical properties of hazard functions focusing on the testing of monotonicity in the context of survival analysis The central contribution is the development of a robust theoretical framework for assessing monotonic behavior in hazard rates derived from censored survival data We derive the asymptotic distribution of a novel test statistic designed to detect deviations from monotonicity rooted in the estimation of hazard functions via nonparametric methods Through a series of simulations we evaluate the performance of our test in terms of power and type I error rates under various models including exponential and Weibull distributions Additionally we provide practical guidelines for application demonstrating the tests utility through realworld datasets Our findings elucidate the nuances of hazard function behavior and offer a rigorous methodology for researchers seeking to understand the implications of monotonicity in survival data The results pave the way for enhanced inferential techniques in the analysis of lifetime data across diverse fields including medicine engineering and social sciences

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In statistical modeling the current status model where observations represent the state of a system at a single point in time poses unique challenges for parameter estimation due to the incomplete nature of the data This paper introduces two novel estimation approaches Maximum Smoothed Likelihood Estimation MSLE and Smoothed Maximum Likelihood Estimation SMLE tailored for the current status model MSLE involves the maximization of a smoothed likelihood function allowing for enhanced estimation robustness by alleviating the impact of noise and irregularities in the data Conversely SMLE employs a twostep framework that first smooths the likelihood surface before conducting the maximization process providing an alternative pathway to parameter estimation Through a comprehensive simulation study we evaluate the performance of both methods in terms of bias variance and computational efficiency We also compare them to traditional estimation techniques demonstrating substantial improvements in parameter recovery and overall model fit across various scenarios characterized by differing sample sizes and underlying distributions Our theoretical results underpin the efficacy of these approaches and provide guidelines for their practical implementation in current status datasets ultimately contributing to more reliable statistical inference in fields where timetoevent data is inherently incomplete

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Asymptotic behavior of large deviations of empirical distribution functions dfs is considered Borovkov and Hoadley obtained results for functionals continuous in the sup norm topology on the set of dfs Groeneboom Oosterhoff and Ruymgaart extended this to functionals continuous in a stronger topology This result is now extended to functionals that are continuous only on a particular useful subset of dfs Applications to the AndersonDarling statistic and linear combinations of order statistics are considered We begin by correcting the work of Abrahamson from this the role of the key weight function t logt t is discovered It is then exploited to the end indicated above and it is considered as a weight function in tests of fit

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: AbstractIn the analysis of current status data with competing risks the estimation of parameters through maximum likelihood estimation MLE presents unique challenges due to the nature of incomplete observations and the existence of competing events This paper investigates the consistency and rates of convergence of the MLE in the context of current status data influenced by competing risks We establish the asymptotic properties of the MLE demonstrating that it is consistent under mild regularity conditions Moreover we derive the rate of convergence showing that it converges at a polynomial rate dependent on the underlying data structure Through simulation studies and realworld applications we illustrate the practical implications of our theoretical findings highlighting how the competing risks framework can affect the efficiency and reliability of MLE in current status analysis Our results provide a solid foundation for future research and methodologies in the statistical analysis of survival data with competing risks enhancing the robustness of parameter estimation techniques in this complex area of study

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Abstract In this paper we introduce a novel methodology for estimating convex functions through the concept of the invelope derived from the integrated Brownian motion combined with a T transformation Our approach builds on the foundational properties of Brownian motion and leverages advanced statistical techniques for convex function estimation We define the invelope as a statistical construct that captures the essential traits of convex functions while accommodating variations induced by stochastic processes Theoretical underpinnings are established demonstrating the consistency and asymptotic normality of our proposed estimator We present simulation studies to illustrate the practical efficacy of our method showcasing its advantages over traditional estimation techniques Furthermore we discuss applications in various domains where convex function estimation is crucial such as economics finance and machine learning The results indicate that our invelope approach provides a robust framework for tackling the complexities of convex function estimation in the presence of noise and uncertainty paving the way for further research in stochastic analysis and convexityrelated problems

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: A process associated with integrated Brownian motion is introduced that characterizes the limit behavior of nonparametric least squares and maximum likelihood estimators of convex functions and convex densities respectively We call this process the invelope and show that it is an almost surely uniquely defined function of integrated Brownian motion Its role is comparable to the role of the greatest convex minorant of Brownian motion plus a parabolic drift in the problem of estimating monotone functions An iterative cubic spline algorithm is introduced that solves the constrained least squares problem in the limit situation and some results obtained by applying this algorithm are shown to illustrate the theory

text: We study nonparametric estimation for current status data with competing risks Our main interest is in the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator MLE and for comparison we also consider a simpler naive estimator Groeneboom Maathuis and Wellner Ann Statist proved that both types of estimators converge globally and locally at rate n We use these results to derive the local limiting distributions of the estimators The limiting distribution of the naive estimator is given by the slopes of the convex minorants of correlated Brownian motion processes with parabolic drifts The limiting distribution of the MLE involves a new selfinduced limiting process Finally we present a simulation study showing that the MLE is superior to the naive estimator in terms of mean squared error both for small sample sizes and asymptotically

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We consider the maximum likelihood estimator of a distribution function in a class of deconvolution models where the known density of the noise variable is of bounded variation This class of noise densities contains in particular bounded decreasing densities The estimator is defined characterized in terms of Fenchel optimality conditions and computed Under appropriate conditions various consistency results for are derived including uniform strong consistency The Canadian Journal of Statistics c Statistical Society of Canada

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper investigates isotonic estimation techniques in the context of Wicksells problem which addresses the challenge of estimating the distribution of radial distances between randomly placed points in a Euclidean space We focus on the application of isotonic regression methods to derive nonparametric estimators that preserve the monotonic structure inherent in the underlying distribution Our primary contribution includes establishing convergence rates for these estimators under different conditions leveraging empirical process techniques and concentration inequalities We provide a detailed analysis of the asymptotic properties and robustness of the proposed estimators including a comparison with traditional parametric approaches Through simulations and theoretical derivations we demonstrate the efficacy of isotonic estimators in achieving improved convergence rates highlighting their potential utility in practical applications where monotonicity is a natural constraint The findings not only contribute to the theoretical understanding of estimation in Wicksells problem but also suggest avenues for further research in related nonparametric estimation challenges

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Summary Let be twosided Brownian motion originating from zero and let Va be defined by Va supt Wt t a is maximal Then is a Markovian jump process running through the locations of maxima of twosided Brownian motion with respect to the parabolas fat t a We give an analytic expression for the infinitesimal generators of the processes a in terms of Airy functions in Theorem This makes it possible to develop asymptotics for the global behavior of a large class of isotonic estimators ie estimators derived under order restrictions An example of this is given in Groeneboom where the asymptotic distribution of the standardized Ldistance between a decreasing density and the Grenander maximum likelihood estimator of this density is determined On our way to Theorem we derive some other results For example we give an analytic expression for the joint density of the maximum and the location of the maximum of the process where c is an aribrary positive constant We also determine the Laplace transform of the integral over a Brownian excursion These last results also have recently been derived by several other authors using a variety of methods

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Some theorems on firstorder asymptotic behavior of probabilities of large deviations of empirical probability measures are proved These theorems extend previous results due to Borovkov Hoadley and Stone A multivariate analogue of Chernoffs theorem and a large deviation result for trimmed means are obtained as particular applications of the general theory

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: It is shown that in the nonparametric setting for the socalled Wicksell problem the distribution function of the squared radii of the balls cannot be estimated at a rate faster than nroot log n We present an isotonic estimator of the distribution function which attains this rate and derive its asymptotic normal distribution It is shown that the variance of this limiting distribution is exactly half the asymptotic variance of the naive plugin estimator

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper investigates the properties of Brownian motion under the influence of a parabolic drift with a specific focus on the connections to Airy functions We first establish the mathematical framework for modeling Brownian motion with a quadratically varying drift term leading to a new class of stochastic processes that exhibit features influenced by both classical Brownian motion and the unique characteristics of Airy functions Through rigorous analysis we derive explicit solutions for the probability density function and transition probabilities of the modified process revealing the intricate interplay between the drift and the underlying stochastic behavior Furthermore we explore the longterm behavior of the system identifying asymptotic properties and moments that provide insights into the impact of the parabolic drift on the trajectory of the particle Our findings contribute to the broader understanding of stochastic processes influenced by polynomial drifts with potential applications in fields such as finance physics and biological modeling By drawing connections between these two mathematical domains we highlight the richness of the structural relationships that govern complex systems

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we investigate the consistency of maximum likelihood estimators MLEs within a broad class of deconvolution models which are frequently employed in various fields such as signal processing and biostatistics to estimate underlying distributions from observed convoluted data We establish conditions under which the MLEs converge in probability to the true parameter values as the sample size increases Our results extend existing frameworks by accommodating a wider variety of kernel functions and error distributions including those with heavy tails By employing tools from empirical process theory and leveraging the properties of convex hulls we provide a robust theoretical foundation for the consistency of MLEs in deconvolution contexts Through simulations and real data applications we illustrate the practical implications of our findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of MLEs in recovering the original signal from contaminated observations These results not only contribute to the theoretical understanding of deconvolution estimators but also pave the way for future research in nonparametric inference and robust statistical methodologies

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we introduce the Bivariate Current Status Model a flexible statistical framework for analyzing bivariate data with current status observations where the exact event times are not observed but the status of each variable is recorded at a specific threshold time Current status data are prevalent in various fields such as medical research reliability engineering and social sciences where the timing of events is critical yet challenging to capture Our model uniquely accommodates the joint analysis of two related survival processes allowing for the exploration of dependency structures and the potential influence of covariates on both dimensions We derive the likelihood function and propose an estimation procedure based on the ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm facilitating the handling of incomplete data We demonstrate the efficacy of our model through simulation studies and apply it to a real dataset to illustrate its practical utility The results reveal significant insights into the interdependencies of the bivariate current statuses thereby enhancing our understanding of complex bivariate phenomena This model expands the toolkit available for researchers dealing with current status data and offers a robust approach to inferential statistics in the presence of censoring and interrelated outcomes

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: For the univariate current status and more generally the interval censoring model distribution theory has been developed for the maximum likelihood estimator MLE and smoothed maximum likelihood estimator SMLE of the unknown distribution function see eg and For the bivariate current status and interval censoring models distribution theory of this type is still absent and even the rate at which we can expect reasonable estimators to converge is unknown We define a purely discrete plugin estimator of the distribution function which locally converges at rate n and derive its normal limit distribution Unlike the MLE or SMLE this estimator is not a proper distribution function Since the estimator is purely discrete it demonstrates that the n convergence rate is in principle possible for the MLE but whether this actually holds for the MLE is still an open problem We compare the behavior of the plugin estimator with the behavior of the MLE on a sieve and the SMLE in a simulation study This indicates that the plugin estimator and the SMLE have a smaller variance but a larger bias than the sieved MLE The SMLE is conjectured to have a nrate of convergence if we use bandwidths of order n We derive its normal limit distribution using this assumption Finally we demonstrate the behavior of the MLE and SMLE for the bivariate interval censored data of which have been discussed by many authors see eg and

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate large deviation principles for empirical probability measures derived from independent and identically distributed iid random variables We establish conditions under which large deviations occur for the empirical distribution function as the sample size tends to infinity By leveraging the relationship between empirical measures and the underlying true distribution we derive exponential bounds characterizing the probability of significant deviations from the expected frequencies of events Our results extend classical large deviation theorems by incorporating convergence results for empirical measures and provide a comprehensive framework for understanding the asymptotic behavior of these measures in the context of various topologies including Wasserstein metrics and weak convergence Moreover we discuss applications of our theorems in statistical inference model validation and information theory illustrating their relevance in practical scenarios The findings contribute to the broader field of probability theory and statistical applications paving the way for future research on robust statistical methodologies in highdimensional settings

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: AbstractIn survival analysis current status data where the event of interest is only observed if it occurs before a certain censoring time poses unique challenges particularly in the presence of competing risks This paper investigates the asymptotic properties of the maximum likelihood estimator MLE for parameters when analyzing current status data in the context of competing risks We derive the limiting distribution of the MLE under various competing risk models providing insights into its consistency and asymptotic normality Simulation studies demonstrate the robustness of our theoretical results and highlight the practical implications for researchers dealing with current status data in medical and social sciences Additionally we apply our findings to a realworld dataset illustrating how to adequately estimate the probability of event occurrence while accounting for competing risks The results emphasize the importance of considering competing risks in the analysis of current status data enhancing the validity of statistical inferences drawn from such studies This work contributes to the broader understanding of survival analysis and offers practical tools for researchers navigating the complexities of competing risks in censored data frameworks

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Abstract In this paper we introduce a novel methodology for estimating convex functions through the concept of the invelope derived from the integrated Brownian motion combined with a T transformation Our approach builds on the foundational properties of Brownian motion and leverages advanced statistical techniques for convex function estimation We define the invelope as a statistical construct that captures the essential traits of convex functions while accommodating variations induced by stochastic processes Theoretical underpinnings are established demonstrating the consistency and asymptotic normality of our proposed estimator We present simulation studies to illustrate the practical efficacy of our method showcasing its advantages over traditional estimation techniques Furthermore we discuss applications in various domains where convex function estimation is crucial such as economics finance and machine learning The results indicate that our invelope approach provides a robust framework for tackling the complexities of convex function estimation in the presence of noise and uncertainty paving the way for further research in stochastic analysis and convexityrelated problems

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: A process associated with integrated Brownian motion is introduced that characterizes the limit behavior of nonparametric least squares and maximum likelihood estimators of convex functions and convex densities respectively We call this process the invelope and show that it is an almost surely uniquely defined function of integrated Brownian motion Its role is comparable to the role of the greatest convex minorant of Brownian motion plus a parabolic drift in the problem of estimating monotone functions An iterative cubic spline algorithm is introduced that solves the constrained least squares problem in the limit situation and some results obtained by applying this algorithm are shown to illustrate the theory

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Interval censoring occurs when the exact value of an observation is not known but rather it is known to lie within a certain interval This phenomenon is common in various fields including survival analysis clinical trials and reliability engineering In this paper we propose new estimators to address the interval censoring problem aiming to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of statistical inference under these constraints We derive maximum likelihood estimators MLEs using both fully parametric and semiparametric frameworks and we assess their performance through asymptotic properties and simulation studies Additionally we introduce a robust Bayesian approach to interval censoring utilizing prior information to refine estimates where data is sparse or heavily censored We compare the proposed estimators to existing methods through extensive simulations under different censoring schemes and sample sizes Our empirical results indicate that our estimators outperform traditional approaches in terms of bias and mean squared error particularly in situations with substantial censoring Finally we present a realworld application to demonstrate the practical utility of our methods in analyzing patient survival data The findings contribute significant advancements to the statistical methodology for handling intervalcensored data providing researchers with improved tools for analysis and inference

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Two test statistics are introduced to test the null hypotheses that the sampling distribution has an increasing hazard rate on a specified interval These statistics are empirical Ltype distances between the isotonic estimates which use the monotonicity constraint and either the empirical distribution function or the empirical cumulative hazard They measure the excursions of the empirical estimates with respect to the isotonic estimates owing to local nonmonotonicity Asymptotic normality of the test statistics if the hazard is strictly increasing on is established under mild conditions This is done by first approximating the global empirical distance by a distance with respect to the underlying distribution function The resulting integral is treated as sum of increasingly many local integrals to which a central limit theorem can be applied The behavior of the local integrals is determined by a canonical process the difference between the stochastic process x bar right arrow Wx x where W is standard twosided Brownian motion and its greatest convex minorant

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper investigates the properties of the concave majorant of standard Brownian motion a fundamental object in stochastic processes and statistical analysis We develop a framework to analyze the concave majorant as a function of time establishing its relationship with the underlying Brownian path By employing techniques from convex analysis we derive new results concerning the distribution and statistical characteristics of the concave majorant In particular we show that the expectation and variance of the concave majorant can be expressed in terms of the local time of Brownian motion Additionally we explore the asymptotic behavior of the concave majorant as the observation window extends providing insights into its scaling properties Our findings reveal a deeper understanding of the role of the concave majorant in the context of stochastic processes and its implications in various applications including option pricing and risk assessment in finance We conclude with potential extensions of this research to multidimensional Brownian motion and discuss the implications for future studies in probabilistic modeling and statistical inference

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper investigates the asymptotic properties of convex hulls generated by random samples from multivariate distributions We establish several limit theorems that describe the behavior of the convex hull as the sample size increases particularly focusing on the cases of independent and identically distributed iid points Using tools from geometric probability and concentration inequalities we derive convergence results for the volume and surface area of convex hulls in both Euclidean spaces and more complex geometrical settings We demonstrate that the distribution of the volume of the convex hull converges to a limiting distribution under appropriate scaling and we provide explicit expressions for the asymptotic mean and variance Additionally we explore the impact of dimensionality on the concentration of measure phenomena related to convex hull structures Our results have implications for various applications including statistical shape analysis computational geometry and the study of random polytopes Theorems are supported by rigorous proofs and accompanied by simulations that illustrate the theoretical predictions We also discuss potential extensions of our results to more general sampling frameworks including stratified and dependent sampling Through this work we contribute to a deeper understanding of the probabilistic underpinnings of convex hulls and their statistical properties paving the way for further research in this emerging area of study

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of functionals derived from the convex hulls of random points in multidimensional spaces We establish limit theorems that characterize the distributional properties of various functionals applied to convex hulls including the area volume and geometric parameters such as the diameter and the shape characteristics of the hulls formed by sequences of independent and identically distributed random variables Utilizing techniques from geometric probability and large deviation theory we derive conditions under which convergence in distribution occurs for these functionals as the number of points approaches infinity Our results extend existing theoretical frameworks and provide new insights into the statistical properties of convex hulls demonstrating how the distribution of functionals behaves under different dimensional contexts and point distributions Numerical simulations are conducted to support the theoretical findings and illustrate practical implications paving the way for applications in fields such as spatial statistics computational geometry and data analysis

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: This paper introduces Generalized Continuous Isotonic Regression GCIR a novel extension of traditional isotonic regression methodologies tailored for continuous response variables across various distributions Isotonic regression is wellestablished for estimating monotonic relationships but existing frameworks often impose limitations on the type of response data they can handle Our approach generalizes the concept by integrating a broader class of loss functions and accommodating nonparametric strategies to maintain monotonicity We rigorously outline the mathematical foundations of GCIR presenting algorithms for efficient computation and convergence guarantees Key theoretical results demonstrate its consistency and robustness in highdimensional settings alongside simulation studies illustrating improved performance compared to standard isotonic methods Applications in fields such as biostatistics and econometrics are utilized to highlight the practical benefits of GCIR offering insights into the underlying trends of realworld data while maintaining a flexible modeling framework This work paves the way for further advancements in nonparametric regression techniques encouraging researchers to explore the implications of continuous isotonic relationships in diverse datasets

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: The standard isotonic regression of a vectorin Rn is the solution to a least squares projection problem on the cone C of vectors with increasing components in Rn Generalized isotonic regression problems are isotonic optimization problems that seem to be quite different from isotonic regression problems but in fact have the same solution In problems of maximum smoothed likelihood estimation often continuous versions of generalized isotonic regression problems emerge In this paper we show that the solutions to such problems are often given by the relatively simple continuous isotonic regression of a function We illustrate the result using the problem of maximum smoothed likelihood estimation of an increasing hazard function C Elsevier BV

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: The asymptotic relative efficiencies of Bahadur and Pitman can be interpreted as limits of a natural smallsample relative efficiency concept In a number of examples the accuracy of the approximation of smallsample efficiencies by asymptotic efficiencies is investigated numerically paying special attention to Bahadur asymptotic efficiencies The more recently introduced asymptotic deficiencies are also considered Although accurate in some cases the asymptotic efficiency in the sense of Bahadur often turns out to be quite an unsatisfactory measure of the relative performance of two tests when the sample sizes are moderate or small On peut interpr ter les efficacit s asymptotiques de Bahadur et Pitman comme limites dune mesure defficacit qui est bien propre pour les chantillons de petites tailles et qui se base sur les nombres dobservations n cessaires pour obtenir une puissance fix e Pour quelques exemples la pr cision de lapproximation est tudi e par moyens num riques Les r sultats laissent penser que tr s souvent lefficacit asymptotique au sens de Bahadur nest pas un outil satisfaisant en cas d chantillons de tailles mod r es Il est possible dintroduire des mesures defficacit de second ordre mais ce moment les r sultats de telles m thodes sont encore tr s incomplets

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we investigate the statistical properties of hazard functions focusing on the testing of monotonicity in the context of survival analysis The central contribution is the development of a robust theoretical framework for assessing monotonic behavior in hazard rates derived from censored survival data We derive the asymptotic distribution of a novel test statistic designed to detect deviations from monotonicity rooted in the estimation of hazard functions via nonparametric methods Through a series of simulations we evaluate the performance of our test in terms of power and type I error rates under various models including exponential and Weibull distributions Additionally we provide practical guidelines for application demonstrating the tests utility through realworld datasets Our findings elucidate the nuances of hazard function behavior and offer a rigorous methodology for researchers seeking to understand the implications of monotonicity in survival data The results pave the way for enhanced inferential techniques in the analysis of lifetime data across diverse fields including medicine engineering and social sciences

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: It is shown that the process of vertices of the convex hull of a uniform sample from the interior of a convex polygon converges locally after rescaling to a strongly mixing Markov process as the sample size tends to infinity The structure of the limiting Markov process is determined explicitly and from this a central limit theorem for the number of vertices of the convex hull is derived Similar results are given for uniform samples from the unit disk

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Interval censoring occurs when the exact value of an observation is not known but rather it is known to lie within a certain interval This phenomenon is common in various fields including survival analysis clinical trials and reliability engineering In this paper we propose new estimators to address the interval censoring problem aiming to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of statistical inference under these constraints We derive maximum likelihood estimators MLEs using both fully parametric and semiparametric frameworks and we assess their performance through asymptotic properties and simulation studies Additionally we introduce a robust Bayesian approach to interval censoring utilizing prior information to refine estimates where data is sparse or heavily censored We compare the proposed estimators to existing methods through extensive simulations under different censoring schemes and sample sizes Our empirical results indicate that our estimators outperform traditional approaches in terms of bias and mean squared error particularly in situations with substantial censoring Finally we present a realworld application to demonstrate the practical utility of our methods in analyzing patient survival data The findings contribute significant advancements to the statistical methodology for handling intervalcensored data providing researchers with improved tools for analysis and inference

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In this paper we explore the concepts of Bahadur efficiency and smallsample efficiency within the framework of statistical inference Bahadur efficiency provides a measure of the asymptotic optimality of statistical procedures particularly in the context of nonparametric hypothesis testing by comparing the rates of convergence of the null and alternative hypotheses In contrast smallsample efficiency focuses on the performance of estimators and tests under limited sample sizes addressing the discrepancies that can arise between theoretical asymptotic properties and practical applications We present an integrated approach to assess both Bahadur efficiency and smallsample efficiency for a variety of commonly used statistical tests and estimators such as ttests and rankbased tests Through a combination of simulation studies and theoretical derivations we highlight the tradeoffs between the two efficiency measures elucidating scenarios where traditional asymptotic results may fail to provide adequate guidance in finite samples Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of statistical procedures effectiveness promoting the careful consideration of sample size in empirical research The insights provided by this study have significant implications for the design of experiments and the interpretation of statistical results in practice

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: In a central limit theorem for the number of vertices of the convex hull of a uniform sample from the interior of a convex polygon is derived This is done by approximating the process of vertices of the convex hull by the process of extreme points of a Poisson point process and by considering the latter process of extreme points as a Markov process for a particular parametrization We show that this method can also be applied to derive limit theorems for the boundary length and for the area of the convex hull This extends results of Renyi and Sulanke and Buchta and shows that the boundary length and the area have a strikingly different probabilistic behavior

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Current status data where the event of interest is observed only at a certain point in time without knowledge of the exact failure time poses unique challenges in statistical analysis This paper introduces likelihood ratio type tests tailored for twosample comparisons in the context of current status data We develop a novel framework that leverages the likelihood ratio statistic to assess differences between two independent groups addressing both the nonobservability of event times and the estimation of survival functions Our approach is grounded in rigorous statistical theory and is applicable to a range of scenarios including medical research and reliability engineering We demonstrate the asymptotic properties of the proposed tests including consistency and asymptotic normality and provide explicit algorithms for the estimation of parameters and test statistics Extensive simulation studies illustrate the performance of the tests in finite samples showing robust power and control of Type I error rates compared to traditional methods Finally we apply our methodology to a real dataset to showcase its practicality and effectiveness in extracting insights from current status data This work contributes significantly to the field of survival analysis by offering a reliable and powerful tool for comparative studies involving censored data

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We introduce fully nonparametric twosample tests for testing the null hypothesis that the samples come from the same distribution if the values are only indirectly given via current status censoring The tests are based on the likelihood ratio principle and allow the observation distributions to be different for the two samples in contrast with earlier proposals for this situation A bootstrap method is given for determining critical values and asymptotic theory is developed A simulation study using Weibull distributions is presented to compare the power behaviour of the tests with the power of other nonparametric tests in this situation

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: Let S t S be a version of the slope at time t t of the concave majorant of Brownian motion on It is shown that the process S S is the inverse of a pure jump process with independent nonstationary increments and that Brownian motion can be generated by the latter process and Brownian excursions between values of the process at successive jump times As an application the limiting distribution of the L L norm of the slope of the concave majorant of the empirical process is derived

author: Piet Groeneboom
text: We study three estimators for the interval censoring case problem a histogramtype estimator proposed in the maximum likelihood estimator MLE and the smoothed MLE using a smoothing kernel Our focus is on the asymptotic distribution of the estimators at a fixed point The estimators are compared in a simulation study
